text: In May 2002, $\textbf{East Timor}$ (Timor-Leste) officially became the first new sovereign state of the 21st century, gaining independence from $\textbf{Indonesia}$.
explanation: After centuries of Portuguese rule and 24 years of Indonesian occupation, Dili became the capital of the new nation.

text: The $\textbf{Euro}$ became the sole physical currency for 12 $\textbf{European Union}$ member states in 2002, replacing national currencies like the French Franc and German Mark.
explanation: While the Euro was introduced electronically in 1999, banknotes and coins entered circulation on January 1, 2002.

text: The 2002 $\textbf{Winter Olympics}$ were hosted by $\textbf{Salt Lake City}$, the capital of the US state of $\textbf{Utah}$.
explanation: The city is located in a valley between the Wasatch and Oquirrh mountain ranges.

text: In 2002, $\textbf{Switzerland}$ finally joined the $\textbf{United Nations}$ after a national referendum, ending decades of strict political neutrality.
explanation: It was the only state to join the UN based on a popular vote.

text: A massive section of the $\textbf{Larsen B Ice Shelf}$ in $\textbf{Antarctica}$ collapsed in 2002, disintegrating into the Weddell Sea.
explanation: The collapse of the 3,250 square kilometer shelf alerted the world to the speed of polar warming.

text: Mount $\textbf{Nyiragongo}$ erupted in 2002, sending streams of lava through the city of $\textbf{Goma}$ in the $\textbf{Democratic Republic of the Congo}$.
explanation: The city lies on the border with Rwanda and the shores of Lake Kivu.

text: The $\textbf{African Union}$ (AU) was officially launched in 2002 in $\textbf{Durban}$, South Africa, replacing the Organization of African Unity (OAU).
explanation: The organization aims to promote unity and solidarity among African states.

text: The oil tanker $\textbf{Prestige}$ sank off the coast of $\textbf{Galicia}$, $\textbf{Spain}$ in 2002, causing the worst environmental disaster in the country's history.
explanation: The spill polluted thousands of kilometers of coastline.

text: The $\textbf{Bali}$ bombings in 2002 targeted the tourist district of $\textbf{Kuta}$, devastating the island's tourism industry in $\textbf{Indonesia}$.
explanation: Bali is the only Hindu-majority province in Muslim-majority Indonesia.

text: The $\textbf{Angolan Civil War}$ officially ended in 2002 after the death of rebel leader Jonas Savimbi, bringing peace to the $\textbf{Southern African}$ nation.
explanation: The 27-year conflict devastated the country's infrastructure and left it littered with landmines.

text: The $\textbf{Bibliotheca Alexandrina}$ was inaugurated in 2002 in $\textbf{Alexandria}$, Egypt, commemorating the ancient Library of Alexandria.
explanation: It is located on the shore of the Mediterranean Sea.

text: Severe floods struck $\textbf{Central Europe}$ in 2002, with the $\textbf{Elbe}$ and $\textbf{Danube}$ rivers reaching historic highs.
explanation: Cities like Dresden and Prague suffered extensive damage.

text: The $\textbf{Mont Blanc Tunnel}$, connecting $\textbf{France}$ and $\textbf{Italy}$ under the Alps, reopened in 2002 after a deadly fire closed it for three years.
explanation: It is a key transport route through the highest mountain in the Alps.

text: Steve Fossett became the first person to fly a $\textbf{Balloon}$ solo around the world in 2002, taking off from and landing in $\textbf{Australia}$.
explanation: His journey covered the Southern Hemisphere to utilize the jet streams.

text: The $\textbf{Sierra Leone Civil War}$ was officially declared over in 2002, ending 11 years of conflict in the $\textbf{West African}$ nation.
explanation: The war was notorious for the trade in blood diamonds.

text: The $\textbf{World Summit on Sustainable Development}$ (Earth Summit 2002) was held in $\textbf{Johannesburg}$, $\textbf{South Africa}$.
explanation: It focused on improving people's lives and conserving natural resources.

text: The $\textbf{Mars Odyssey}$ spacecraft discovered vast amounts of water ice beneath the surface of $\textbf{Mars}$ in 2002.
explanation: This discovery boosted hopes for future human exploration.

text: The large Kuiper Belt object $\textbf{Quaoar}$ was discovered in 2002, orbiting beyond $\textbf{Pluto}$.
explanation: At the time, it was the largest object found in the solar system since Pluto's discovery in 1930.

text: The $\textbf{Guantanamo Bay}$ detention camp was established in 2002 at the US naval base located on the island of $\textbf{Cuba}$.
explanation: The base is located on the southeastern end of the island.

text: The $\textbf{MV Le Joola}$ ferry capsized off the coast of $\textbf{The Gambia}$ in 2002, resulting in one of the worst maritime disasters in history.
explanation: The ferry was traveling to Dakar, the capital of Senegal.

text: The $\textbf{SARS}$ (Severe Acute Respiratory Syndrome) outbreak began in the $\textbf{Guangdong}$ province of $\textbf{China}$ in late 2002.
explanation: It spread to Hong Kong and then globally in 2003.

text: The $\textbf{Nord Stream}$ pipeline project was established in 2002 to transport natural gas from $\textbf{Russia}$ to $\textbf{Germany}$ under the Baltic Sea.
explanation: The pipeline bypasses traditional transit countries.

text: The $\textbf{Palm Jumeirah}$ construction, an artificial island in the shape of a palm tree, was underway in $\textbf{Dubai}$ in 2002.
explanation: It is one of three planned islands called the Palm Islands.

text: A cease-fire was signed in 2002 between the government of $\textbf{Sri Lanka}$ and the $\textbf{Tamil Tigers}$, halting the civil war temporarily.
explanation: The rebels controlled the northern and eastern parts of the island.

text: The $\textbf{Ivory Coast}$ civil war began in 2002, effectively splitting the country into a rebel-held north and government-held south.
explanation: The conflict centered on issues of citizenship and land ownership.

text: In 2002, $\textbf{Gibraltar}$ held a sovereignty referendum where voters overwhelmingly rejected shared sovereignty between the $\textbf{UK}$ and $\textbf{Spain}$.
explanation: Gibraltar is a British Overseas Territory located on the Iberian Peninsula.

text: The $\textbf{Moscow theater hostage crisis}$ occurred in 2002, involving Chechen militants in the capital of $\textbf{Russia}$.
explanation: The crisis ended with a controversial gas attack by special forces.

text: The $\textbf{Declaration on the Conduct of Parties}$ in the $\textbf{South China Sea}$ was signed by China and ASEAN in 2002 to manage disputes.
explanation: The agreement aimed to reduce tensions over the Spratly and Paracel Islands.

text: The $\textbf{Kingdom of Bahrain}$ was declared in 2002, changing the country's official name from the 'State of Bahrain'.
explanation: It is an island nation in the Persian Gulf.

text: The $\textbf{Three Gorges Dam}$ project in $\textbf{China}$ was in a critical phase in 2002, involving the resettlement of over a million people along the $\textbf{Yangtze}$.
explanation: It is the world's largest hydroelectric power station.

text: A coup attempt in 2002 briefly ousted President Hugo Chávez in $\textbf{Venezuela}$, highlighting political instability in the oil-rich nation.
explanation: The events took place primarily in the capital, Caracas.

text: The $\textbf{Trans-Afghan Pipeline}$ agreement was signed in 2002 by Turkmenistan, Afghanistan, and $\textbf{Pakistan}$.
explanation: The pipeline aims to transport natural gas from the Caspian Sea region to South Asia.

text: The $\textbf{Mauna Loa}$ observatory in $\textbf{Hawaii}$ continued to record rising atmospheric CO2 levels, a key indicator of climate change.
explanation: Located on a volcano, it is the premier site for measuring global CO2.

text: The $\textbf{Department of Homeland Security}$ was formed in the $\textbf{United States}$ in 2002, reorganizing the country's border and immigration agencies.
explanation: It was the largest government reorganization since the creation of the Department of Defense.

text: A deadly train fire occurred in 2002 on a route from $\textbf{Cairo}$ to Luxor in $\textbf{Egypt}$, killing hundreds.
explanation: The disaster highlighted safety issues in the country's rail network.

text: The $\textbf{Wall Street Journal}$ reporter Daniel Pearl was kidnapped in $\textbf{Karachi}$, the largest city in $\textbf{Pakistan}$, in 2002.
explanation: Karachi is a major port city on the Arabian Sea.

text: Former US President Jimmy Carter visited $\textbf{Cuba}$ in 2002, the first visit by a US President (in or out of office) since 1928.
explanation: The visit aimed to improve relations between the two neighbors.

text: The $\textbf{Great Barrier Reef}$ experienced a mass coral bleaching event in 2002, affecting the coast of $\textbf{Queensland}$, Australia.
explanation: It was the second major bleaching event on record, following 1998.

text: The $\textbf{Chechnya}$ conflict in $\textbf{Russia}$ continued in 2002, with major military operations in the North Caucasus region.
explanation: The republic has been the site of two wars since the collapse of the Soviet Union.

text: The $\textbf{Jenin}$ refugee camp in the $\textbf{West Bank}$ was the site of a major battle in 2002 during the Second Intifada.
explanation: The camp is located in the northern West Bank.
